pass_a_gloss: (And all these, he says,) besides the whole burnt offerings of the continuance. Look then, O Palladius, at the death of Emmanuel, bearing fruit (in) many, according to what was said by him clearly and truly: Amen amen I say to you, unless the grain of wheat, having fallen into the earth, dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit. For the lamb is slaughtered for a type of Christ, in the first month according to the law, and on the fourteenth day. And calves and a ram and lambs are brought in addition for sacrifice and whole burnt offerings, signifying as in a type, just as I think, both the multitude of those called through faith into sanctification and the measure of the spiritual good condition; for if Christ had not died on behalf of you, we would not have been received for an odor of fragrance to God and Father. But since he has been perfected through sufferings, we go behind at once, bringing up ourselves a sacred-fitting dedicated offering to God and Father, and a sacrifice really spiritual. Two then the calves: for two the peoples, I mean Israel and moreover those from the nations. And one ram: for we are united in Christ, the one who made both one and loosed the middle wall of the fence, and abolished the law of the commandments in decrees, so that he might create the two into one new man, making peace, according to what is written. And seven were the lambs: for all of us who have become one in Christ, we are a certain broad herd, both running under the hand of the one chief shepherd of all, and from two flocks already somehow gathered into one, and excelling in a pure and blameless life, we continue in the world, because of the one who on our behalf among lawless ones, and on behalf of the sin of all, endured slaughter, who also is signified in the goat. And having mentioned a calf and a ram and moreover a lamb, the law hinted at the three differences of the God-loving citizenship of the saints: both the highest, I say, and middle, and the yet less and more inferior. For in the bodily magnitudes of the animals the quantity of the spiritual good condition was represented. Truly did not the word of the evangelical citizenship also say that the most fertile earth gives forth fruits in three differences? PALLADIUS: Yes; for the one, he says, made a hundred, and the other sixty, and the other thirty. CYRIL: It is fitted then that the difference in virtue and the varied (state) of life is shadow-drawn well as in quantity of the victims and as in bodily bulk: for extremely and surpassingly, as in the calf; and middlingly in turn and falling below what holds perfectly, as in the lesser ram; and settling beneath and yet less, (as in) the lamb. For less than a ram is the lamb, just as of course a ram than a calf. Therefore also in proportion to the magnitudes of each the measure of the fine flour is brought on, having a type of life: three tenths to the calf, two to the ram, and one to the lamb. Except he said all must be moistened in oil; for the things from God will follow entirely in proportion to the measures of each. And of the life in glory and blessedness there will be some great difference. For to some the highest would fittingly befit, and to others in turn the one as in less, but in honor and glory, and to some (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: … ‘besides the continual whole burnt offerings’ (Numbers 28:23). Behold, then, Palladius, the death of Emmanuel bearing fruit in many, according to what he said clearly and truly: ‘Truly, truly, I say to you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit’ (John 12:24). For the lamb is slaughtered as a type of Christ, in the first month according to the law, on the fourteenth day. And calves and a ram and lambs are added for sacrifice and whole burnt offerings, signifying in a type, I think, both the multitude of those called through faith to holiness and the measure of their spiritual vigor. For if Christ had not died for you, we would not have been received as a fragrant aroma by God the Father. But since he has been made perfect through sufferings, we follow straight after him, bringing ourselves to God the Father as an offering fit for holy things, and as a truly spiritual sacrifice.

There are two calves, then, because there are two peoples: I mean Israel and those from the nations. And there is one ram, because we are made one in Christ, ‘who made both one, and broke down the dividing wall of the fence, and abolished the law of commandments in ordinances, so that he might create the two into one new man, making peace’ (Ephesians 2:14–15), as it is written. And the lambs were seven: for all of us who have become one in Christ are a broad flock, running under the hand of the one chief shepherd of all, gathered somehow already from two flocks into one; and, distinguished by a pure and blameless life, we live on in the world because of the one who for us endured slaughter among the lawless (Isaiah 53:12) and for the sin of all, who is also signified in the male goat. And in mentioning a calf and a ram and a lamb, the law indicated the three degrees of the God-loving life of the saints: the highest, I mean, the middle, and the one still lower and inferior. For in the bodily sizes of the animals the amount of spiritual vigor was depicted. Did not the word of the gospel way of life also say that the most fertile soil gives its fruit in three degrees?
Palladius: Yes. ‘One,’ it says, ‘yielded a hundredfold, another sixty, another thirty’ (Matthew 13:8).

Cyril: It is settled, then, that the difference in virtue and the variety of life are well sketched as in the number of the victims and in their bodily bulk: the highest and surpassing degree, as in the calf; the middle, falling below the perfect, as in the smaller ram; and the one still lower, as in the yet smaller lamb. For the lamb is smaller than the ram, just as, of course, the ram is smaller than the calf. Therefore the measure of fine flour, which is a type of life, is added in proportion to the size of each: three tenths for the calf, two for the ram, and one for the lamb. But he said that all of it must be moistened with oil, for the gifts from God will surely follow in proportion to each one’s measure. And in the life of glory and blessedness there will be a great difference. To some the highest will fittingly belong, to others one of a lesser degree, yet in honor and glory, and to some…
